question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit child agent profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported security boundary?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes which workspace files default child subagents can read, so automation should not decide the workspace isolation policy.

options.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where safe isolation requires configured child agent profiles and `requireAgentId` when default same-agent spawns should be blocked.

options.title: Add Narrow Opt-In Config
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` only as an opt-in same-agent default-child override with schema, docs, doctor/security review, and focused tests.

options.title: Defer To Broader Workdir Design
options.body: Hold this until subagent workspace, `cwd`, sandbox, and skill workdir isolation are designed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where safe isolation requires configured child agent profiles and `requireAgentId` when default same-agent spawns should be blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checked lines and recent subagent/config history point to this person as the best available router for the product/security boundary decision.
